INTRO.INTRO1.speaker: narrator
INTRO.INTRO1.text: America, the 1880s. Hundreds of thousands of people from around the world have moved to the big cities of the Northeast. You are among them. You have come to pursue the American dream of freedom and prosperity. But your dream has not yet come true. You cannot find a job. Other new Americans work long hours for low pay in steel mills, factories and coal mines. On a cold February day, you wander the streets looking for work. Suddenly something catches your eye that will change your life forever. Come to Kansas where the land is free, where the water is pure, where every farmer is prosperous and as independent as a king. Ride the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe line to Kansas and raise your family in paradise. You take a chance and decide to board a train going west. Your family, husband, wife and five-year-old daughter is on its way to a new life. Railroad lines stretched across the country to connect east and west. Isolated settlements of the Great Plains were finally linked to the rest of the country. People flocked to the area to take advantage of new opportunities in agriculture, industry and trade. Along the way, you stop in the cities that are growing along the railroad lines, canals and rivers.
